To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DELLAs act as transcriptional hubs that integrate multiple signaling pathways to coordinate the response of plants to environmental cues.
DELLA proteins act together with cytokinin-responsive type-B ARRs to regulate transcription and that this mechanism is important for the regulation of root meristem size and photomorphogenesis.
DELLAs are recruited to the promoter of genes by specific transcription factors, in particular by type-B ARRs, where they act to activate their transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new regulatory mechanism by which DELLAs integrate hormonal signals with the transcriptional machinery.
the identification of a transcriptional co-activation mechanism that links the DELLA and cytokinin signaling pathways.
the elucidation of transcriptional networks in plants, which are mediated by DELLA proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DELLA proteins interact with transcriptional factors to regulate gene expression in response to environmental cues.
DELLAs and type-B ARR proteins are transcriptional co-actuators of cytokinin-regulatable gene expression.

DELLA proteins act at the transcriptional level by recruiting transcription factors from different gene families to the promoters of their target genes, where they serve as transcriptional coactivators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DELLA proteins act in a similar fashion to the co-activators of animal transcription factors.
DELLAs act as hubs that connect multiple transcriptional circuits to relay environmental information.
DELLAs act as hubs for transcriptional regulation of growth and development through the physical association to different families of transcription factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DELLA proteins can act as coactivators for the cytokinin signaling pathway, which provides a molecular explanation for their ability to integrate environmental cues into growth and development.
DELLA proteins act in a highly specific manner to integrate environmental cues into the transcriptional machinery.

DELLA proteins can act as hubs to coordinate transcriptional responses to multiple stimuli, and that they can be integrated in the same transcriptional circuit to provide plasticity to plant responses.
